questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Two events $A$ and $B$ are such that $P(A)=\dfrac{8}{15}$, $P(B)=\dfrac23$ and $P(A\cap B)=\dfrac15$.

Find:

(a) $P(A\cup B)$, *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Addition rule: $P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B)$. With a common denominator $15$:

$$P(A\cup B)=\frac{8}{15}+\frac{10}{15}-\frac{3}{15}=\frac{15}{15}=1.$$

**$P(A\cup B)=1$.**

$B$ is split into the part in $A$ and the part not in $A$: $P(B)=P(A\cap B)+P(A'\cap B)$. Hence

$$P(A'\cap B)=P(B)-P(A\cap B)=\frac23-\frac15=\frac{10-3}{15}=\frac7{15}.$$

**$P(A'\cap B)=\dfrac7{15}$.**

Conditional probability: $P(A'\mid B)=\dfrac{P(A'\cap B)}{P(B)}$.

$$P(A'\mid B)=\frac{7/15}{2/3}=\frac7{15}\times\frac32=\frac{7}{10}.$$

**$P(A'\mid B)=\dfrac7{10}=0.7$.** (Check: $P(A\mid B)=\frac{1/5}{2/3}=\frac{3}{10}$ and $\frac3{10}+\frac7{10}=1$.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii) In a given class, 40% of the students are boys and 60% are girls. Given that 20% of the boys and 30% of the girls are short sighted. A student $X$ is chosen at random from the class. By drawing a tree diagram or otherwise, find the probability that:

(a) $X$ is short sighted, *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Tree diagram.** First branches: Boy $0.4$, Girl $0.6$. From Boy: short sighted ($S$) $0.2$, not short sighted ($S'$) $0.8$. From Girl: $S$ $0.3$, $S'$ $0.7$.

| Path | Probability |
|---|---|
| Boy and $S$ | $0.4\times0.2=0.08$ |
| Boy and $S'$ | $0.4\times0.8=0.32$ |
| Girl and $S$ | $0.6\times0.3=0.18$ |
| Girl and $S'$ | $0.6\times0.7=0.42$ |

(The four probabilities add up to $1$.)

$$P(S)=0.08+0.18=0.26.$$

**The probability that $X$ is short sighted is $0.26=\dfrac{13}{50}$.**
themes: tree diagrams and conditional probability (additional maths)

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) $X$ is a girl or short sighted, *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Use $P(G\cup S)=P(G)+P(S)-P(G\cap S)=0.6+0.26-0.18=0.68$.

(Check with the tree: the only outcome that is neither a girl nor short sighted is "Boy and $S'$" with probability $0.32$, so $1-0.32=0.68$.)

**The probability is $0.68=\dfrac{17}{25}$.**
themes: tree diagrams and conditional probability (additional maths)
